They copy a post from there that included a youtube link (or any link i think) and just replace it with their onlinevideo link. item.title: West Virginia pastor rejects food over LGBQT support. Now his food bank is empty.
item.description: Alvin Christian is the man behind God’s Store House Food Bank in Bluefield, West Virginia, a city located in the southernmost part of the state. Since 2023, the pastor has helped feed up to 800 families a day. If you’ve ever worked at a food pantry, you know donations can come from individuals, larger food banks, or local businesses with excess product they can’t sell anymore. As recently as last week, Christian was letting supporters know everything he had in store for them. But he recently filmed a video showing viewers that his freezers were completely empty. There was no food coming in, and therefore no food going out. In the now-deleted reel, Christian explained that there were outlets trying to give him the resources he needed… he just refused to take them. Because, after doing his own research, he found out those groups worked with or supported LGBTQ people. A copy of the video was preserved by Facebook user nes.quick.737, who said the pastor “would rather let his people STARVE than to accept food for the pantry from the LGBTQ community.” https://www.friendlyatheist.com/p/west-virginia-pastor-rejects-food

item.title: GovBrief Today #551
item.description: Kansas beat the anti-abortion movement twice in two days. On Monday, Judge Christopher Jayaram issued a 260 page ruling that the state cannot force women to wait 24 hours or answer questions about their finances or their reasons before ending a pregnancy. He wrote that under the Kansas Constitution's guarantee of bodily autonomy, his ruling was not even a close call. Hours later he was sworn onto the Kansas Supreme Court. On Tuesday, voters crushed a ballot amendment its backers planned to use to ban abortion by remaking that court. The ruling permanently blocks enforcement. Kansas can still appeal, but that appeal goes to a state Supreme Court that has already ruled bodily autonomy fundamental. The restrictions are gone as long as Kansans keep guarding the court that killed them, which is exactly what they did on Tuesday. item.title: Crispy Edge Pan Pizza.
item.description: Crispy Edge Pan Pizza ( by LetsCookie on Reddit/r/FoodVideoPorn ) Dough Ingredients 350 g (2½ cups) bread flour 227 g (1 cup) water 9 g (1 tsp) fine salt 2.5 g (¾ tsp) instant yeast 7.5 g (1½ tsp) olive oil 5 g (1 tsp) granulated sugar Sauce 1 (28 oz) can crushed tomatoes 1 tsp dried oregano 1 tsp fine salt ½ tsp granulated garlic 2 tsp granulated sugar 2 TB olive oil Toppings Freshly grated Parmesan cheese Low-moisture whole milk mozzarella, shredded (I used Grande) Method Add the water, sugar, and instant yeast to the bowl of a stand mixer. Stir together and let sit for about 10 minutes, until the yeast becomes active and foamy. Add the bread flour, salt, and olive oil. Knead with the dough hook for 8–10 minutes, or knead by hand until smooth and elastic. Lightly oil a large bowl with olive oil. Transfer the dough to the bowl and form it into a smooth ball by pulling the dough underneath itself and pinching the bottom closed. Place it seam-side down so the smooth side is facing up. Cover tightly with plastic wrap and let rise until doubled in size. Lightly coat a 10 x 14-inch Lloyd pan (or similar deep rectangular pan) with 2–3 tablespoons olive oil. Transfer the dough to the pan and gently stretch it toward the edges. If it keeps shrinking back, cover it and let it rest for 10–15 minutes so the gluten can relax, then continue stretching it until it reaches the corners. Cover again and let the dough proof in the pan for about 2 hours. Use a dough docker or a fork to dock the dough all over to help prevent large bubbles. Spread on a thin, even layer of sauce, leaving about a ½-inch border around the edges. Sprinkle generously with freshly grated Parmesan cheese, then cover with a generous amount of shredded low-moisture whole milk mozzarella. Bake at 550°F for about 12 minutes, or until the cheese is golden brown and the edges develop a deep, crispy caramelized crust. Let cool for 1-2 minutes before removing from the pan, slicing, and serving. Notes : The sauce recipe makes more than you need for one pizza. Freeze the extra for another batch. Grande whole milk mozzarella is excellent if you can find it at GFS or Restaurant Depot. Otherwise, use any good-quality low-moisture whole milk mozzarella. That crispy cheese edge is the star of this pizza, so don't be afraid to let the edges get deeply browned before pulling it from the oven.
